title: Explain 'pre-registered' where it appears
description: Readers see 'pre-registered' on dimension and question pages without an explanation. Add a short inline definition (accessible tooltip or expandable note) and a methods-page section: before an engine answered anything, each prediction (direction and rough size) was committed to the public repository, so the commit date proves it came first; the page then shows prediction, observed result and verdict. Link each prediction's commit. Distinguish pre-registered questions from exploratory ones.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Feature: Pre-registration explained in place
  Scenario: A reader meets the term
    Given a page that labels a question or cell 'pre-registered'
    When the reader hovers, focuses or taps the label
    Then a plain-language definition appears and links to the methods section
  Scenario: The prediction's date is provable
    Given a pre-registered prediction on a page
    Then the page links the commit that recorded it, dated before the engine's first answer

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Feature: Results first
  Scenario: Public pages show results, not hypotheses
    Given any dimension, group, question, cell or engine page, or its social card
    When it is built
    Then it shows no 'pre-registered' label, no prediction and no verdict
    And it leads with the measured result, its interval and an example
  Scenario: The method is still auditable
    Given the methods page
    Then one sentence says predictions were committed before each run and links to the repository's pre-registration files

comments.author: home
comments.text: 2026-09-23: done on main (Haiku pass A, reviewed): Prereg blocks, labels, verdicts and card lines removed from public pages; methods page has one sentence and a repository link.

right_now_summary: Public pages now show results only, while the methods page explains pre-registration and links to the repository.
